title.en: Bijection, cycle derivation and orientation beyond position

summary: Confirm the move permutation is a bijection, that displayed cycles come from the engine, and that position alone is not solved state.
objective: The permutation is bijective, displayed cycles match the engine decomposition, and restored positions with changed orientation are not reported as solved.
applies_when: A scene displays where pieces travel under a move or sequence.
Cycle notation or arrows are drawn alongside the puzzle.
Pieces carry orientation in addition to position.
intent_signals: two pieces ended in the same slot
the cycle arrows disagree with the move
example_prompts: Check the permutation cycles shown for this move sequence.

principles: A move is a bijection on slots: every source appears once and every destination appears once, which is checked before any cycle display is drawn.
Cycle decomposition is derived from the same permutation the engine applies; a separately authored cycle animation can drift from the model it claims to describe.
Position is not the whole state, because pieces can return to their slots with changed orientation, so a cycle display alone cannot report a solved puzzle.
implementation: Build the mapping from source slot to destination slot and verify that the image set equals the domain set exactly.
Derive cycles by walking unvisited slots and confirm that cycle lengths sum to the number of moved pieces plus the listed fixed points.
Compose a sequence and compare the cycle structure derived from the composed permutation with the structure obtained by composing cycles, so display and engine agree.
Construct a case where every piece returns to its slot while at least one orientation differs and record what the interface reports.
observable_checks: The permutation is a bijection with each slot appearing exactly once as source and once as destination; a repeated destination identifies pieces being overwritten.
Cycles derived from the engine permutation match the displayed cycles element for element, including fixed points.
The all-positions-restored case with a changed orientation is not reported as solved; reporting it as solved is the failure this check exists for.

known_limits: Positional cycle checking does not validate whether a state is reachable by legal moves, which needs a complete puzzle model.
Authored verification guidance; no puzzle implementation was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: Every permutation is a product of disjoint cycles, and cube notation that names the facelets of a piece in order records where the piece goes together with its twist, so position alone does not encode orientation.
claims.scope: Finite permutations of puzzle piece positions as described in the cited page; not a validity test for arbitrary puzzle states.

source_refs.locator: Disjoint cycle decomposition and the facelet ordering that specifies piece twist
